aiReview.summary: Mfinity is visually above average and technically clean, but it is not yet reference-quality for luxury car rental. The cinematic direction and accessible booking entry point are credible; the largest commercial gaps are missing trust proof, an ambiguous reservation outcome, incomplete pricing context, and imagery that obscures rather than showcases the vehicles. The page also spends too much of its first viewport on atmosphere and brand language relative to concrete local service value. Scores are intentionally below the automated results because the visible experience does not yet support the high-confidence, high-value booking decision expected in Marbella and Puerto Banús.
strengths: The brand has a coherent cinematic luxury direction, with restrained monochrome UI, strong contrast, and a location cue for Marbella.
The first viewport does include both vehicle discovery and an availability form, so the critical booking journey is findable rather than buried.
The featured vehicle card provides a concrete model, daily starting price, and deposit, giving the proposition more substance than a purely lifestyle-led luxury site.
The responsive composition remains structurally intact on mobile: no horizontal overflow, large tap targets, and a prominent availability action are supported by the objective scan.
The technical foundation is strong: fast loading, low layout shift, valid status, complete image alt coverage, canonical metadata, sitemap/robots support, and no console or network errors.

aiReview.summary: Trenes y Tranvías has a strong first impression and a more distinctive visual identity than a generic professional-services template. The real vehicle imagery, memorable headline and restrained editorial styling establish a credible specialist direction. The main weakness is commercial: the site looks ready to generate interest but does not yet provide enough proof, operational detail or direct contact infrastructure to convert high-consideration buyers. The absence of a visible enquiry mechanism and trust signals is the largest gap against the lead-generation goal. Mobile craft is acceptable for the hero itself, but the oversized composition and small secondary controls reduce efficiency. Overall, this is a promising branded homepage rather than reference-quality professional-services execution.
strengths: The hero immediately communicates the product category with a real, relevant tourist-train image rather than generic stock imagery.
The visual direction is distinctive: black, white and warm yellow create a coherent transport-and-city identity, while the serif emphasis on “a bordo” adds personality.
The headline is memorable and emotionally aligned with tourism and place-making.
The page has a clear high-level structure around cities and tourism, events and celebrations, and companies and spaces.
The primary CTA language is action-oriented and appropriate for a project-based sales journey.
The site is technically fast and stable according to the scan, with no horizontal overflow, failed requests, console errors or broken internal links.
The Écija/Sevilla reference provides a useful starting point for local relevance, even though broader service coverage is not yet made clear.

issues.title: The mobile hero strands the primary enquiry action below an oversized static summary
issues.detail: On the supplied mobile viewport, the page opens with the brand, a tall text-heavy hero, and a large four-part charter summary. The "Find my charter" button visible on desktop is not visible within the mobile first viewport; the panel consumes roughly the lower half of the screen and appears as fixed values rather than immediately operable controls.
issues.evidence: The mobile screenshot shows Guests, Duration, Departure, and The Day extending to the bottom of the 1680px capture without a visible enquiry action. The scan also records 25 undersized interactive targets out of 43.
issues.observed: A mobile visitor must scroll beyond a large prefilled form summary before reaching the conversion action, with no immediate indication of how to edit the selections.
issues.expected: Reference-quality mobile luxury travel booking surfaces place a clear enquiry/availability action within or directly following a compact, obviously editable trip summary, preferably above the fold.
issues.location: Homepage, mobile hero and charter selector
issues.recommendation: Reduce the mobile selector to a compact summary or progressive flow; make each field visibly interactive; and keep a full-width "Check availability" or "Plan my charter" CTA permanently visible at the end of the visible module. Use touch targets of at least 44px for every field and navigation action.

issues.title: The hero image does not deliver a decisive luxury-charter visual promise
issues.detail: The only supplied hero image is a busy Puerto Banus marina composition dominated by apartment facades, masts, mooring lines, and overlapping vessels. It establishes place, but it does not let a prospective guest inspect a distinctive yacht, onboard setting, coastline, or charter moment.
issues.evidence: Both desktop and mobile screenshots use the same dense marina image. The objective scan reports only 2 images across the page despite fleet and experience-led discovery being central to the offer.
issues.observed: The page reads more as a destination editorial than an exclusive yacht-charter proposition. On mobile, the serif headline and body copy also sit over high-detail architecture and rigging, reducing visual calm and legibility.
issues.expected: A reference-quality luxury charter homepage uses original, cinematic but informative imagery: a hero vessel underway or an unmistakably premium onboard moment, supported by a purposeful visual sequence for vessels, experiences, and destinations.
issues.recommendation: Replace or rotate the hero with commissioned/original charter imagery that clearly shows the product and setting. Build a fuller image system around real vessel exteriors, deck/interior details, guests, crew, and local coastline. Apply the minimum contrast treatment necessary to preserve image quality while making type reliably readable.

issues.title: There is no visible trust layer for an expensive private charter decision
issues.detail: The homepage makes an experience and local-expertise claim, but the scan finds no trust signals. There are no visible guest reviews, rating source, operational credentials, safety/insurance reassurance, named expertise, press, partner affiliations, or evidence of completed charters.
issues.evidence: The objective scan records trustSignalCount: 0. The hero claims "more than fifteen years of local experience," but the supplied screens do not substantiate it.
issues.observed: A visitor is asked to make an enquiry for a high-ticket leisure service based largely on brand language and a phone number.
issues.expected: Reference-quality operators provide concise, credible proof close to enquiry points, without compromising the premium tone.
issues.location: Homepage hero and primary enquiry path
issues.recommendation: Add a restrained trust strip and supporting proof near the charter CTA: verified review rating/source, years operating, licensed/insured or safety credentials where applicable, concierge response expectation, and a small number of authentic client or partner signals. Link to fuller proof rather than overcrowding the hero.

issues.title: Touch targets and text scale are materially under-sized for mobile use
issues.detail: The navigation and secondary links are styled with very small type and shallow hit areas. This makes an already high-consideration browsing task less comfortable on touch devices.
issues.evidence: The scan reports a tinyTapTargetRatio of 0.5, with 25 of 43 interactive elements measured as small. It also reports 62 tiny-text elements (28.8% of visible elements), including 8.8px to 11.5px labels, links, contact information, and yacht metadata. Desktop navigation links are measured at 12.5px by roughly 20px high.
issues.observed: Important secondary navigation and informational labels rely on fashion-editorial scale at the expense of scanning and tap confidence.
issues.expected: Reference-quality mobile luxury sites can retain restraint but use durable text sizing and 44px-or-larger interactive hit areas, especially for navigation, contact, discovery links, and booking controls.
issues.location: Header navigation, hero discovery link, secondary text links, fleet metadata, and mobile menu
issues.recommendation: Raise interactive targets to at least 44px high, increase practical body and metadata sizes, and preserve visual refinement through spacing, weight, case, and hierarchy rather than sub-12px type. Ensure the mobile menu trigger and its expanded links meet the same standard.

issues.title: The central promise is elegant but generic and under-explains the charter offer
issues.detail: "Marbella, from the water" is a strong destination line, but the supporting copy bundles private yacht charter, sailing, fishing, and group experiences together. That breadth reduces the sense of a carefully curated luxury service and gives little concrete reason to choose this operator over nearby alternatives.
issues.evidence: The H1 and hero copy in the screenshots and scan emphasize broad activity categories. Homepage word count is 551, and only 2 images are present to substantiate the categories or craft a differentiated story.
issues.observed: The page prioritizes atmospheric language over distinctive product proof such as vessel quality, crew/service level, itinerary expertise, or what is included.
issues.expected: Reference-quality luxury positioning pairs concise aspiration with specific, verifiable differentiators and clear audience/product segmentation.
issues.location: Homepage hero and introductory story section
issues.recommendation: Keep the location-led H1, but tighten the supporting proposition around the actual premium offer: curated fleet standard, experienced local crew/concierge, key departure points, and the types of charters the business specializes in. Separate yacht charters from fishing or group formats so the latter do not dilute the premium primary message.

issues.title: A broken About link interrupts credibility research
issues.detail: The About destination is part of the internal navigation path but fails according to the scan. For an unfamiliar charter provider, company background is a key reassurance route before an enquiry.
issues.evidence: brokenInternalLinkRatio is 0.0833, with https://marbellaboatcharter.vercel.app/about.html identified as broken.
issues.observed: Visitors following "Our approach" or seeking company credentials can reach a dead end rather than the information that should establish legitimacy.
issues.expected: All credibility and discovery links should resolve to complete, polished pages, particularly on an enquiry-led premium site.
issues.location: Homepage "Our approach" path / About page link
issues.recommendation: Restore the About page at the linked URL or update every reference to the correct live route. Validate the complete internal-link set in the deployment build.

issues.title: The interface has a polished direction but lacks enough distinctive product-led craft to justify luxury positioning
issues.detail: The overall treatment uses familiar premium-editorial cues: a translucent dark header, oversized high-contrast serif headline, spaced all-caps labels, off-white panels, thin rules, and black CTA block. These are competently assembled, but with minimal proprietary imagery or visible bespoke service detail, they create a somewhat template-like luxury aesthetic.
issues.evidence: The screenshot shows repeated editorial conventions, while the scan reports only 2 images and 33 colors. The header, hero, and charter panel carry most of the visual experience rather than a developed product-specific visual system.
issues.observed: The design signals "premium website" before it signals why this particular Marbella charter operator is distinctive.
issues.expected: Reference quality feels authored around the real fleet, hospitality standard, local access, and photography, with repeatable components that visibly belong to the operator.
issues.recommendation: Retain the restrained typographic framework but make it more ownable through a richer original image art direction, vessel-specific visual modules, authentic operational details, and a more characteristic brand device than generic rules and letter-spaced labels alone.

aiReview.summary: The site has a credible editorial foundation: a restrained palette, a polished serif/sans pairing, local Marbella positioning, and a fast, technically sound enquiry path. It does not yet reach the visual or commercial standard expected of a luxury yacht-charter operator. The mobile first viewport is dominated by promotional copy and a very tall prefilled charter panel whose action is out of view; imagery is limited and the primary image presents a dense marina rather than a clearly aspirational charter experience. Trust proof is notably absent, and a broken About link weakens a high-consideration purchase journey.
strengths: The desktop hero establishes the Marbella and Puerto Banus location immediately, with a clear brand lockup and prominent "Plan a charter" action.
The desktop charter configurator gives useful decision context up front: guests, duration, departure, and type of day. This aligns well with the enquiry-led charter journey.
Typography has an intentional editorial direction rather than relying entirely on default SaaS styling. The display serif helps signal premium positioning.
The site supports fleet, experience, destination, owner, contact, and booking discovery, giving the business an appropriately broad information architecture.

The objective scan indicates strong operational fundamentals: no horizontal overflow, zero layout shift, accessible labels and image alt text, no console or network failures, and fast desktop/mobile LCP.
Fleet cards expose starting prices and practical vessel details, which is valuable pricing context for a high-consideration service.

issues.observed: A high-intent visitor is shown branding and imagery before being given a clear next action.
issues.expected: A premium real-estate home page should make the next meaningful action unmistakable while retaining an editorial presentation: immediate search/discovery and a discreet but clear adviser-enquiry route.
issues.location: Homepage hero, desktop and mobile first viewport.
issues.recommendation: Add a concise, high-contrast hero action such as 'Explore residences' linked to filtered inventory, plus a secondary 'Speak with an adviser' action. On mobile, retain one visible text CTA above the fold rather than making all navigation-dependent.

issues.title: Property discovery is deferred behind branding and navigation
issues.detail: For a platform whose secondary goal is property discovery, the opening surface does not expose a search field, location, budget, property type, featured residence metadata, or visible inventory signal. 'Exceptional homes' exists only later in the document outline.
issues.evidence: The screenshots show no filter or search control. The DOM does contain a later H2, 'Exceptional homes', and only 7 current residences, but no above-fold property-discovery affordance is visible.
issues.observed: The visitor must infer that the site has listings and use navigation or scroll to begin browsing.
issues.expected: Reference-quality premium agency sites balance visual storytelling with a fast route to a relevant set of homes, particularly for international buyers arriving with area and budget intent.
issues.recommendation: Introduce an understated search rail or compact discovery entry point with area, property type and budget, or make a featured property module visibly begin within the initial scroll cue.

issues.title: No visible trust or adviser proof supports a high-consideration enquiry
issues.detail: There is no visible evidence in the first screen of who represents the buyer, why the agency is qualified in Marbella, how quickly it responds, or what happens after contact. This is a material omission for premium residential transactions where the site asks visitors to trust an unknown local intermediary.
issues.evidence: The objective scan reports trustSignalCount: 0 and bookingSignalCount: 0. The screenshots contain brand text, navigation and imagery only.
issues.observed: The brand looks premium, but the claim is unsupported at the point where confidence must begin.
issues.expected: The first journey should quickly connect the inventory to credible local expertise through an adviser identity, established local credentials, media/partner recognition where genuine, client proof, or a concrete concierge service proposition.
issues.location: Homepage hero and immediately following content.
issues.recommendation: Place a concise credibility cue adjacent to the main action or directly beneath the hero, then substantiate it in the next visible section with real local credentials and named-adviser access.

issues.title: Hero typography prioritizes brand scale over property-specific storytelling
issues.detail: The oversized, widely spaced wordmark is visually confident, but it occupies the central focal area without naming a location, property type, service distinction or current inventory. On mobile it becomes the dominant content over a largely anonymous crop of the villa.
issues.evidence: Both screenshots feature only 'MARBELLA FOR SALE' as the central hero message. The DOM H1 is 'Marbella, chosen well.', but that messaging is not visible in the provided hero state.
issues.observed: The hero resembles a premium campaign splash screen more than an agency homepage designed to start a considered property journey.

aiReview.summary: The opening image is polished and appropriately aspirational, with a convincing luxury-real-estate tone. However, the first viewport functions more as a brand film still than a property-discovery or enquiry surface. It does not establish a tangible reason to engage, provide a visible route into search, or supply the credibility and local expertise expected of a premium Marbella adviser. The exceptionally high automated measurements confirm a technically clean baseline, but the visible product and conversion craft do not yet justify reference-quality scores.
strengths: The full-bleed dusk villa image immediately communicates the market, price tier and aspirational intent without looking like a generic SaaS or portal template.
The restrained white type, darkened image treatment and generous canvas create a coherent editorial luxury direction.
Desktop and mobile preserve a clean, uncluttered first impression; the mobile layout has no visible overflow and the hero lettering remains legible.
The information architecture is broad and relevant to the business: properties, developments, areas, seller services, insights, about and contact are all present in the navigation.

Technical signals are notably strong: no failed requests or console errors were found, core performance metrics are excellent, all images have alternative text, and internal links and form action are present.

issues.title: Privacy notice overwhelms the primary booking moment
issues.detail: The cookie/privacy layer occupies roughly a quarter of the desktop viewport and more than a third of the mobile viewport. On mobile it covers the lower hero, including the point at which the primary page CTA would normally be encountered. It becomes the dominant call to action before the restaurant proposition or booking choice can be evaluated.
issues.evidence: Both supplied screenshots show the notice on initial load. In the mobile screenshot, the dialog spans nearly the full width and extends from roughly two-thirds down the screen to the bottom; the hero headline is visibly cut behind it. The objective scan confirms that booking itself is available, so the issue is not journey failure but first-screen interference.
issues.observed: A mandatory-looking privacy interface visually competes with the header's RESERVAR action and obscures the hero content.
issues.expected: Reference-quality hospitality sites keep legally required consent concise and subordinate, preserving a legible view of the venue, value proposition and main booking action on first arrival.
issues.location: Homepage initial viewport, desktop and mobile.
issues.recommendation: Reduce the notice to a compact, low-height banner or a tightly sized modal with a clear close affordance. Preserve privacy/legal access in the banner while allowing the hero CTA and key venue information to remain visible; ensure its mobile height does not cover the primary content zone.

issues.title: Mobile hero fails to protect the key message and booking context from overlap
issues.detail: The mobile composition has limited vertical room for the label, award text and large display headline. The cookie layer then sits over the lower portion, leaving "Mar de verdad." partially hidden and preventing a complete first-screen reading of the promise. The booking button is available in the header, but the intended hero conversion path is not visibly available.
issues.evidence: In the mobile screenshot, only "Mar de" and part of the next line are visible above the privacy dialog. The page's hero CTA visible on desktop, "RESERVAR MESA", is not visible on mobile because the overlay occupies that area.
issues.observed: The mobile viewport presents atmosphere, a large partial headline and an interrupting dialog, rather than a complete, scannable reservation proposition.
issues.expected: A premium mobile restaurant landing screen should show the brand/place, a complete value statement and one unambiguous booking route together without content collision.
issues.location: Homepage hero at the supplied mobile viewport.
issues.recommendation: Recompose the mobile hero with a defined safe area below the navigation, use a smaller or differently positioned display headline, and keep a persistent visible booking CTA in the hero when consent UI is present. Test the accepted and unaccepted-consent states at common short mobile heights.

issues.title: The award claim lacks enough visible credibility to function as a trust signal
issues.detail: "BEST OF THE BEST 2025" is visible alongside the location label on mobile, but the awarding body is not named. In a premium dining context, an unattributed superlative can read as promotional decoration rather than independently earned proof.
issues.evidence: The screenshot contains the standalone uppercase phrase "BEST OF THE BEST 2025" with no visible source, badge, publication or explanatory context. The scan reports only one trust signal across the page.
issues.observed: The claim asks the visitor to infer authority without being able to identify or verify it.
issues.expected: Reference-quality trust proof identifies the source and makes its relevance intelligible, for example through a recognizable award mark, publication name, rating platform, press quote or a contextual link.
issues.location: Homepage mobile hero, aligned to the right of the Puerto Banus/Marbella location label.
issues.recommendation: Name and, where permitted, show the issuing organization or recognizable mark; link to the relevant recognition or move the proof into a compact credibility section with other independently verifiable signals.

issues.title: Hero image is less crisp and appetizing on mobile than the positioning demands
issues.detail: The mobile hero crop is visibly soft and dominated by empty place settings, a large planter and dark foreground chair forms. It conveys setting, but the restaurant's food and service quality are not visually legible. The desktop crop is more balanced, yet still foregrounds glassware and furniture over a distinctive dish or service moment.
issues.evidence: The supplied mobile image appears blurred/soft at the waterfront edge and table setting, while the central crop shows a large planter and empty tables. Across both screenshots, there is no visible food hero image despite the culinary proposition.
issues.observed: The first image establishes location but provides limited appetite appeal or product evidence.
issues.expected: For an editorial premium restaurant, the hero should pair a recognizable sense of place with an impeccably sharp, intentional food, table or hospitality focal point that rewards close inspection.
issues.location: Homepage hero, most pronounced at mobile viewport.
issues.recommendation: Use an art-directed mobile-specific crop or asset with sharper subject detail and a clear culinary/service focal point. Retain the sea view, but make the food, plating or lived dining experience visible in the first viewport.

issues.title: The first screen under-communicates practical visit confidence
issues.detail: The page leads with a strong poetic line and the location, but opening hours, exact waterfront/address context and menu cue are not visible in the supplied first screens. Those are core decision inputs for destination diners choosing where to reserve in Puerto Banus.
issues.evidence: The objective scan confirms contact signals and links to Carta and Contacto exist, but the screenshots' initial viewport shows no opening-hours information, address/location detail beyond "Puerto Banus · Marbella", or visible menu discovery cue in the mobile navigation state.
issues.observed: Visitors receive brand mood first and must navigate away or continue scrolling to answer basic visit-planning questions.
issues.expected: Premium hospitality sites can remain editorial while giving nearby, low-friction reassurance about where it is, when it operates and what is offered before asking for commitment.
issues.location: Homepage initial viewport, particularly mobile where the navigation is collapsed.
issues.recommendation: Add a concise operational proof point adjacent to the booking route or immediately below the hero, such as today's service hours, a specific waterfront/location descriptor and a compact Carta link. Keep it visually restrained so it supports rather than dilutes the editorial hero.

issues.title: CTA language and treatments are not fully consolidated
issues.detail: The visible site uses "RESERVAR" in the header and "RESERVAR MESA" in the hero, while the privacy dialog introduces two large, visually forceful button styles and a blue text link. The scan also records an inconsistent button ratio of 0.43. Some variation is appropriate by context, but the booking system would feel more precise with one dominant reservation label and stronger visual hierarchy relative to secondary actions.
issues.evidence: Desktop shows an outlined RESERVAR header control and a filled RESERVAR MESA hero control. Mobile shows a filled RESERVAR header control. The objective scan reports an inconsistentButtonRatio of 0.4286.

issues.location: Homepage header and hero across desktop/mobile.
issues.recommendation: Standardize the booking label and establish one clearly primary reservation treatment across header and hero. Keep secondary navigation, consent and utility controls visibly distinct from the conversion action.

aiReview.summary: La Bocana has a strong editorial starting point: a credible waterfront image, restrained palette, distinctive serif display type and a highly visible reservation route. It falls short of reference-quality premium restaurant execution because the first visit is dominated by a large privacy dialog, especially on mobile, and the hero does not immediately convert its atmosphere into sufficiently clear practical decision information. The automated fundamentals are excellent, but the visible first-screen experience is weaker than those scores suggest.
strengths: The hero photography immediately establishes a real waterfront dining setting rather than relying on generic luxury visual language. This is appropriate for Puerto Banus and supports the restaurant's premium positioning.
The desktop masthead is composed with discipline: brand, navigation, language, telephone number and reservation action are all present without a visually noisy header.
Typography has a deliberate editorial contrast. The large serif headline and spaced sans-serif utility labels feel more bespoke than a standard restaurant template.
Reservation is consistently available in the header on both desktop and mobile. The mobile treatment is especially prominent and easy to identify.

The scan supports a strong baseline for the reservation journey and site hygiene: no failed requests, no horizontal overflow, no undersized tap targets, no console errors, fast LCP, and no layout shift.

Core discovery routes are represented in the navigation, including menu, location/contact, gallery and restaurant story. The page also has Spanish language metadata and localized Puerto Banus/Marbella messaging.

issues.detail: The captured desktop and mobile experiences show only a dark burgundy background with a small loading spinner. No property, location, agency identity, service proposition, or local expertise is visible.
issues.evidence: Both supplied screenshots contain no visible content beyond the spinner. The DOM scan reports a word count of 3, zero images, zero navigation links, zero forms, zero CTAs, and only 6 visible elements.
issues.expected: A premium real-estate homepage should immediately establish Inmobiliaria Noguera, its Écija/Sevilla expertise, and the properties or service pathway that justifies a high-value enquiry.
issues.location: Entire first viewport on desktop and mobile
issues.observed: The page presents as an apparently stalled loading state rather than a real-estate website.
issues.recommendation: Fix the initial rendering path so the branded hero, property discovery entry point, and primary enquiry action render reliably without requiring an unresolved loading state. Add a meaningful fallback if data or assets fail to load.
issues.title: The website is effectively blank at first load

issues.detail: There is no visible route to the primary business outcome: a property enquiry. The user cannot contact the agency, request a viewing, ask about a listing, or submit their requirements.
issues.evidence: The scan reports primaryCtaCount 0, formCount 0, contactSignalCount 0, and bookingSignalCount 0. The screenshots show no CTA or contact affordance.
issues.expected: The primary action should be explicit and persistent enough to support high-intent browsing, such as “Solicitar visita”, “Consultar propiedad”, WhatsApp, phone, or a concise enquiry form tied to each property.
issues.observed: No conversion path exists in the rendered interface.
issues.recommendation: Introduce a prominent enquiry CTA in the header/hero and property detail views, plus a low-friction contact option and clear success/error states. Preserve the enquiry context when users originate from a specific property.

issues.detail: The color treatment alone cannot carry the intended editorial, aspirational and luxurious visual direction. A full-viewport flat burgundy field with a small spinner reads as an application loading screen, not as a considered real-estate composition.
issues.evidence: The screenshots show an uninterrupted dark burgundy surface and a small orange loading arc, with no typography, imagery, layout rhythm, or brand mark. The objective color count is only 6, consistent with an extremely sparse rendered surface.
issues.expected: Luxury real estate should use a restrained but dimensional system combining strong typography, generous spacing, credible imagery, and a clear visual hierarchy that makes the property the first-viewport signal.
issues.observed: The visual identity is indistinguishable from an unresolved loading overlay and provides no designed content to evaluate or trust.
issues.recommendation: Replace the blank state with the actual branded composition. Make a relevant property or place image the dominant first-viewport signal, pair it with disciplined editorial typography, and keep the burgundy accent as a supporting brand color rather than the entire experience.

aiReview.summary: This is not currently reviewable as a functioning premium real-estate experience. Both supplied viewports are dominated by an unresolved loading state, and the scan confirms that the rendered document contains virtually no business content or user journey. The measured performance and baseline accessibility results are positive, but they cannot offset the absence of property discovery, enquiry conversion, imagery, trust, and semantic content. The current first-viewport experience is a critical release blocker; the reported automated visual score is not representative of the visible business experience.
strengths: The objective scan indicates a fast, stable delivery path when the page responds: HTTP 200, no failed requests, no console errors, no horizontal overflow, and a valid viewport configuration.

The automated checks report strong baseline accessibility mechanics, including no tiny tap targets, no unnamed buttons, no unlabelled form controls, and complete image-alt coverage for the zero images currently rendered.
The supplied visual palette is restrained and could become a credible premium brand foundation once paired with real content, typography, and property imagery.
